text:
anya: Quick sync — I saw sustained KV cache growth on node-12 during the longctx perf job (8k tokens). Low-traffic tenants started getting paged out.
sam: Do you have the heap/memstat dump? repro steps?
anya: Pasted memstat + short log below. Happened after ~30m of continuous longctx with mixed tenants. Memory kept creeping rather than stabilizing.

```
node: node-12
time: 2026-03-17T15:04:10Z
kv_resident_bytes: 68.3GB -> 81.9GB over 30m
fragmentation_est: 12.6%
eviction_ops: 1243 (mostly background)
per-tenant residency: tenant-a: 45GB, tenant-b: 18GB, tenant-c: 12GB, others: 6GB
```

padma: ugh. that residency skew + fragmentation smells like slab reuse failure for repetitive long sequences. can you share the request patterns? are they same prompt prefixes (good candidate for reuse) or many distinct prefixes?
anya: mix. tenant-a is a chatty LLM with long-conversation reuse opportunities; tenant-b/c are short but frequent. tenant-a's KV entries are often large and only partially reused.

derek: recent kernel selection change (PR #4478) introduced a new kv page allocator path that prefers fixed slab sizes for speed. could be causing internal fragmentation when tenants allocate many medium-size entries.
sam: /repro cmd I used earlier:
```
./run_longctx_repro --nodes node-12 --tenants tenant-a,tenant-b,tenant-c --seq-len 8000 --qps 25 --duration 40m
```
Try adding `--kv-compact-interval=60s` to see immediate effects.

anya: ran with compact-interval=60s. memory still trended down very slowly vs baseline. compaction run shows a lot of short-lived pages freed but large slabs stayed pinned.

infra-bot: alert: node-12 kv-memory-pressure HIGH (85%) — auto-scale not possible for Dedicated pool.

padma: proposal: two-pronged fix:
- add tenant-aware residency cap (soft watermark + reclaim hook)
- implement per-slab freelist coalescing for medium-size allocations to reduce fragmentation

sam: +1 to tenant-aware cap. we can enforce `max_resident_per_tenant` and trigger proactive eviction of least-recently-used entries for that tenant. that would avoid noisy neighbor stealing.
derek: quick experiment toggling allocator flag `--kv-merge-medium-slabs=true` improved fragmentation on local repro (fragmentation_est went 12% -> 4% after 10m). command I ran:
```
kv_allocator_ctl --node node-12 --set merge_medium=true
# wait 10m
kv_metrics_dump | jq '.fragmentation_est, .resident_bytes'
```
results: fragmentation_est=4.1%, resident_bytes: 72.2GB -> stabilized

anya: promising. how does that affect tail latency / CPU? any kernel-side slowdown from merging?
derek: measured ~2% CPU uptick on the allocator path, tail latency unchanged for generation requests. overall token throughput same.
sam: we should still add a per-tenant soft cap to avoid single-tenant growth. ops can roll soft cap first, then enable merge flag cluster-wide in a canary.

ops-bot: scheduled canary: eng-runtime-canary-1 on node-12 window 2026-03-18T02:00-03:00Z
padma: I'll open a small follow-up PR that adds metrics we need for acceptance: `kv.per_tenant_resident`, `kv.slab_merge_events`, and `kv.proactive_evictions`. link: https://git.redwood/infra/pr/4521
anya: thanks. after the merge flag + soft cap on canary, I'll re-run the longctx job and post numbers.

sam: tiny nit: add a telemetry tag for `repro/longctx` so we can filter the metrics in console.

derek: noted. also leaving a TODO to audit kernel selection PR (#4478) for allocator interaction — maybe revert allocator path choice if merge approach proves brittle.
anya: cool, thanks everyone. status: canary scheduled, PR in flight, I'll update after the next run. :thumbsup:
